chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who has two owned slaves, and one of them killed his companion. Does he have the right to exact retaliation against him for that without the ruler, if he wishes that? He said: “He is his property; he may do with him whatever he wishes. If he wishes, he kills, and if he wishes, he pardons.”
ai.seo_question: Can a master carry out retaliation on his slave for killing another slave without the ruler's authority?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a master whose slave kills another of his slaves. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that the owner has authority over the killer slave and may either kill him or pardon him, without requiring the ruler's intervention in this case.
